content.title: About
content.content: Baked beans are a canned dish made from white beans cooked in a tomato‑based sauce with sugar, salt, and spices. They have a sweet‑tangy flavor, soft texture, and are commonly served as a side or a standalone meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Baked beans originated in the United States in the early 19th century as a miners’ staple.
Traditional recipes include molasses, mustard, and spices such as paprika and cloves.
The beans used are usually white (navy) or large varieties, which are high in protein.
In the United Kingdom, “baked beans on toast” is a classic breakfast.
Canning allows the product to be stored for 2‑3 years without refrigeration.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: A serving (≈130 g) provides about 6‑7 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals help form hemoglobin and support nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Baked beans contain virtually no saturated fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, folate, and niacin assist in converting food into energy.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Traditional sauce contains added sugar, which can be an issue for diabetics or those limiting sugar.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Canned versions often contain a lot of salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baked beans can be served hot as a side dish, added to chili, casseroles, salads, or spread on toast. They are also easy to heat in the microwave or on the stovetop with a splash of water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer to a sealed container, refrigerate, and consume within 3‑5 days. Discard if the smell turns sour or the can is bulging.
